about: The review key (R-450). Every row Denning was shown of the engine's plays: what the engine said then (shown), his mark and his words (said), and checks: Claude's reading of his mark as things the plays must hold or must not hold, which he corrects. Scored by tools/golden/review.py on the branch after every change. Marks: right, partly, wrong, bad example (set aside), not marked. Set 1 is the 35 rows of 2026-11-13, picked one or more to a kind of play, so it is a regression test and not an accuracy figure; whole-game sets (R-454) give the accuracy by kind of play. `answered` holds a later answer of his on a row (what was asked, his words, Claude's reading). Set w1p1 is part 1 of the whole-game review (R-455), marked by him on the site on 2026-11-13 against engine af952c6: one row a situation with his mark and words, its calls under `calls` with theirs, and one `missed` row a game for what the engine did not read; checks are written as each fault is fixed. Set w1p2 is hdm v hook, the first game of part 2, marked on 2026-11-14 against engine 67e87b8 as the first measure of the rebuilt reading; he then chose to build from it too, keeping Men v Crew unmarked as the hidden game. Set w2 is round 3 (R-473): hook v hold and cope v Team, marked on 2026-11-14 against engine b025445 (24 of 41 and 15 of 24 situations right); chic v 戦戦戦戦 was set aside unmarked (a henchman game). RJT v RACK (eea5ba87) is round 3's third game, marked on 2026-11-14 against engine b09a26a (33 of 45 situations right); its checks are written from his words and are open until the reading under them is rebuilt. Set p2 is twelve picked rows of 2026-11-18 (R-495: examples found by search for a fault seen once, put to him in the chat with their replay links): six of the two held flag shapes and three sudden deaths of a solo split player. They carry no grade, so none binds; their games are in the development set. Set c1 is the flag advice cards he corrected on Model > Game review > Flag advice (marked 2026-11-20, 61 cards of the twelve f1 games against engine cb7c78a: 58 told correctly, 2 partly, 1 incorrect; all 61 marks are in data/model/flag_card_marks.json): one row a corrected card, with his words and the check on the play the card is written from. They carry no grade, so none binds.

answered.said: at 5:13, hdm derv caps a flag, and then on his own, runs all the way back to flag spawn, picks it up at 6:13, at caps at 7:25. This is a classic single run, no one else is involve. hooks #7 goes back for a flag around 6:07, caps flag at 7:11, and then mesmer of hook is ALREADY on the way to run the next flag, essentially being able to pick up the flag faster than hook's #7 ever could because he is going back towards the flag spawn right after #7 caps. those two flag plays from hook involve two people and gained flag time by sacrificing a bit of player time. I see this as a double run, full run though it's not the clearest example.
